This is the third application under Section 483 of B.N.S.S. for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.270/2024 registered at Police Station Timarni, District Harda (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n), 376(3) of IPC and Sections 3/4(2), 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 18.12.2024.
Previous bail applications were dismissed as withdrawn.

2. As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the present applicant is that he taken away the minor prosecutrix without permission of her parents on the pretext of marriage and committed rape upon her.
On the basis of which, offence has been registered against the applicant under the aforesaid sections.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.

He is in custody since NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50679 2 MCRC-39445-2025 18.12.2024.
It is submitted that the prosecutrix herself went with the applicant.
The prosecutrix is major.
Date of birth of the prosecutrix is not proved as per legal provision.
It is further submitted that the statements of the prosecutrix and her mother have been recorded in which they have not supported the prosecution story.

In support of his contention, learned counsel placed reliance upon the judgment of Division Bench of this Court passed in the case of Prince Chauhan vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh and others vide order dated 20.05.2024 in Cr.A. No.12540/2023.

sentences.text: The conclusion of trial will take considerable time.
Hence, it is prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and has submitted that as per the Higher School certificate, date of birth of the prosecutrix is 04.02.2009 and the date of incident is 26.05.2024, hence at the time of incident, the age of the prosecutrix was Amit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139046038/
1 below 16 years.

entities.text: Amit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that minute appreciation of evidence cannot be done at this stage.
Hence, the applicant does not deserve grant of bail.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
6.

In the case of Satish Jaggi Vs. State of Chhattisgarh, (2007) 11 SCC 195, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "at the stage of granting of bail, the Court can only go into the question of prima facie case established for granting bail, it cannot go into the question of credibility and reliability of witnesses put up by the prosecution.

entities.text: Satish Jaggi Vs. State of Chhattisgarh, (2007) 11 SCC 195
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The question of credibility and reliability of prosecution witnesses can only be tested during trial."
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50679 3 MCRC-39445-2025 7.
Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case as well as the act of applicant, I am not inclined to grant regular bail to the applicant.
8. Accordingly, present MCRC stands dismissed.
